record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: In the homogenized theory of suspensions of solid particles in a fluid, can the evolution of the microstructure lead to particle shocks or collisions, and how should such effects be incorporated together with possible compressibility effects?

artifact.status_search_result: No general homogenized theory incorporating particle shocks/collisions together with compressibility effects appears in the literature. Existing works on homogenization of suspensions (e.g. Höfer and collaborators, and the EMS monograph "Homogenized Models of Suspension Dynamics") treat dilute or moderately dense regimes without resolving particle-shock singularities, while jamming-front and shock phenomena are studied phenomenologically in rheology. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Homogenized Models of Suspension Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph on homogenized models for suspensions, focusing on effective equations without a general treatment of particle shocks and compressibility.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art homogenized models for suspensions do not provide a unified framework including particle shocks/collisions and compressibility.

status_evidence.title: Toward a fluid mechanics of suspensions
status_evidence.snippet: Review describing impact-activated jamming fronts and shock-like phenomena in suspensions, treated phenomenologically.
status_evidence.claim: Shock-like behavior in suspensions is observed and modeled phenomenologically, but not derived from rigorous homogenization with compressibility.
